method: Compare five authored scenario families, eight seeds (100-107), five sizes. Evaluate every complete ledger from a cold history start with unchanged Stack-d5 and Auto.

Three initial families use varied shopping interests; routine variants favor groceries, dining, fuel and pharmacy. The in-store variant assumes 3.5% of ordinary payments are online, versus 16% or 36% in the other families.

All families include expensive legitimate purchases and small frauds. Amounts, rates and labels are assumptions fixed in generation, not empirical estimates. Model outcomes influence whole-candidate selection, never row removal or relabeling.

Broader public candidates use eight evenly spaced cohorts of 4/16/40/120/240 accounts for the five sizes, chronological windows around the first fraud, retaining all rows in each window and at most 2.5% fraud (minimum cap two rows). 32 eligible windows were scored.
Select high F1, verify false alerts and recall together, then inspect rendered graphs. F1 balances precision and recall; selection is not an unbiased performance estimate.
Choose the best F1 candidate per size. At 50 rows use seed 104 over tied 101 because it has more shared merchants and distinct connections.
MCC is retained as the scoring category; readable merchant_category labels are added for graph names without changing model inputs.
Render the 250/1000/5000/10000 finalists in the actual application; review the small example during final library validation. No layout or model changes were needed.

assumptions: USD and UTC are adapter conventions. Source timestamps have no timezone.
Each file starts its own history; no hidden warmup or label feedback is supplied.
Known fraud labels are used for selection and evaluation only, never scoring.
Sparkov has no channel, status, device, or merchant geography fields for this adapter; those remain unknown. Customer location is not merchant location.
Sparkov display names omit its universal fraud_ merchant prefix; stable source merchant identities are preserved.
